Change which regions are drawn inside a view

Source: R/atlas_utils.R
drawing_manipulation.Rd

Verbs that prune depictions, each by a different criterion:

Usage

atlas_view_remove_region(
  atlas,
  pattern,
  match_on = c("label", "region"),
  views = NULL
)

atlas_view_remove_small(
  atlas,
  min_area,
  views = NULL,
  scope = c("region", "piece"),
  labels = NULL,
  exclude = NULL
)

atlas_prune_weak(atlas, threshold = 0.5, weights = NULL)

atlas_view_select(atlas, threshold = 0.5, weights = NULL)

Arguments

atlas

A ggseg_atlas object

pattern

Character pattern to match. Uses grepl(..., ignore.case = TRUE).

match_on

Column of core to match against: "label", the default, or "region". label is the identifier that is unique within an atlas and stable across them, so every verb that selects rows by name or pattern reads it unless told otherwise.

views

Character vector of view names or patterns. Multiple values are collapsed with "|" for matching.

min_area

For atlas_view_remove_small(): minimum area to keep. What it applies to depends on scope; with the default scope = "region" context geometries are never removed.

scope

Whether min_area applies to a label's whole geometry in a view ("region", the default) or to each disconnected piece ("piece").

labels, exclude

For atlas_view_remove_small(): optional regex scoping which labels are considered. labels restricts removal to matching labels, exclude spares them. Only one may be given. Useful with scope = "piece", where a thin structure such as a cortical ribbon has legitimately small pieces that should not be treated as specks.

threshold

For atlas_prune_weak(): minimum share, between 0 and 1, of a region's best-view area that a view must hold to keep drawing it. Higher values are more aggressive.

weights

For atlas_prune_weak(): optional named numeric vector of per-view multipliers applied before comparing areas. Overrides the automatic hemisphere-coverage weighting for the views named.

Value

Modified ggseg_atlas object

Details

  • atlas_view_remove_region(): by name

  • atlas_view_remove_small(): by absolute area

  • atlas_prune_weak(): by area as a share of the region's best view

None of these adds a view, and none removes a region from core: the region stays and is still legended, while its depiction in some view goes. A view can still disappear as a consequence — atlas_prune_weak() drops a view that keeps no region, and the other two drop a view whose last remaining geometry they removed.

atlas_view_remove_small() and atlas_prune_weak() are the same operation asked two ways, an absolute area against a share of the region's largest appearance, with one difference that decides between them: atlas_prune_weak() keeps every region in at least one view, while atlas_view_remove_small() with the default scope = "region" can take a region's geometry out of every view, leaving it legended but drawn nowhere — and the higher the threshold, the more regions that happens to. Check atlas_undrawn() after raising min_area.

For views as objects, see view_manipulation; to remove a region from the atlas altogether, region_manipulation.

Functions

  • atlas_view_remove_small(): Remove geometry below a minimum area threshold. With scope = "region" (the default) a label's whole geometry in a view is removed when its combined area is too small, and context geometries (labels not in core) are never removed. With scope = "piece" individual disconnected pieces are removed while the rest of the region stays – use this to clear stray specks left by volumetric projection. A region's largest piece anywhere in the atlas is always kept, so no region disappears – a speck in one view goes when the same region is drawn properly in another. Context is cleaned too. Optionally scope to specific views. Views are re-packed via atlas_view_gather() in case any view shrank.

  • atlas_prune_weak(): Keep each region only in the views that show it well.

    A slice or projection slab catches a structure in cross-section as readily as along its length, so most regions leave a sliver in most views. That leaves every panel cluttered and every region drawn several times over. A region is kept only where it is substantially represented: in any view holding at least threshold of the area it reaches in its best view.

    Regions are compared as a whole, across all the labels that share a region in core, so bilateral structures stay together – assigning left and right independently splits pairs across panels, which reads as an error rather than a choice. Every region is guaranteed to survive in at least one view, and context geometry (labels absent from core, such as a cortical outline) is never touched.

    Single-hemisphere views are the awkward case: a sagittal panel cuts one hemisphere while axial and coronal panels show both, so on raw area it loses every comparison and empties out. Such views are detected from the hemispheres actually present in each view and their areas scaled to match, so they compete fairly. Pass weights to override.

  • atlas_view_select(): Deprecated. Use atlas_prune_weak(): the old name read as the verb for choosing which views an atlas keeps, which is atlas_view_keep(), and not for choosing which views draw a region.

See also

atlas_manipulation for the other groups

Other atlas manipulations: atlas_core_add(), atlas_manipulation, atlas_structure_reorder(), region_manipulation, relabel_atlas(), view_manipulation

Examples

dk() |> atlas_view_remove_small(min_area = 10)
#> ℹ Removed 10 geometries below area 10
#> 
#> ── dk ggseg atlas ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Type: cortical
#> Regions: 35
#> Hemispheres: left, right
#> Views: inferior, lateral, medial, superior
#> Palette: ✔
#> Rendering: ✔ ggseg
#> ✔ ggseg3d (vertices)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>    hemi                  region                      label
#> 1  left                bankssts                lh_bankssts
#> 2  left caudalanteriorcingulate lh_caudalanteriorcingulate

#> 4  left          corpuscallosum          lh_corpuscallosum

#> 10 left        isthmuscingulate        lh_isthmuscingulate

#> 1  banks of superior temporal sulcus     temporal
